headline: Bab Gas Cap main plant: three bidding teams named
name: Bab Gas Cap development
notes: Research 23 Nov: the bid deadline was extended four months to 16 Nov 2026. Package 1 is the largest of four EPC packages. Construction Review reports four consortiums bidding but the names are not in free sources; MEED reported a Tecnimont and CPECC team forming earlier (unconfirmed for this package). The named list is in MEED's paid article.

Research 24 Nov: per MEED, Worley was awarded the FEED for the Bab gas cap plant in the December before the EPC expressions of interest went out (10 Feb 2026). Worley is the FEED contractor, not a bidder. Bidder names still not in free sources.

Research 26 Nov: Construction Review lists three EPC bidding teams for package 1: (1) L&T Energy Hydrocarbon with Petrofac Emirates; (2) Technip Energies, JGC and Sinopec; (3) Tecnimont with CPECC. MEED also reported the Tecnimont and CPECC team in April. The same article speaks of four consortiums; the fourth is not named. This is secondary reporting: it is unconfirmed which teams submitted technical bids on 16 Nov.
Bidders are not named in public sources yet. Finding the bidders list is the next step. Contractors most often seen on ADNOC Onshore work: Mannesmann Energy, Jereh.

headline: Bab gas cap well tie-ins: 99 wells, a separate project from the Bab and North East Bab oil tie-ins
name: Bab Gas Cap well tie-ins
notes: Research 24 Nov: the tie-in scope is split into 18 EPC packages; MEED has put the budget at $800m-plus and, in an earlier report, $1.2bn. MEED reported on 27 Oct that contractors were selected for a 'Bab and North East Bab One' tie-in project, without naming them; it is unconfirmed whether that is the same tender. No bidders named in free sources.

Research 27 Nov, correcting the 24 Nov note: this $800m-plus project ties in 99 new gas cap wells (60 producers, 39 injectors) from reservoirs KH-2, SH-1 and LK-1. The $1.2bn budget and the 27 Oct 'contractors selected' report belong to a different project, the Bab and North East Bab oil well tie-ins. Which of the two is split into 18 EPC packages is not clear from the summaries. No bidders named.

headline: Jereh's three ADNOC Onshore contracts: values, scope and signing
name: Ruwais Diyab unconventional gas development
notes: Research 24 Nov: Jereh's Shenzhen filing of 4 Nov describes letters of award for three ADNOC Onshore projects worth about $2.7bn (AED9.9bn); formal contracts were not yet signed. The three include Ruwais Diyab (a design, build and operate contract, per MEED sources; ADNOC took FID on 2-3 Nov) and Bab / North East Bab onshore facilities. MEED separately reports a $392m (AED1.44bn) EPC award to Jereh for wellhead surface facilities; whether it is one of the three is unconfirmed.

Research 26 Nov: the three are Ruwais Diyab ($1.7bn: design, build, commission, then operate and maintain for five years), Bab / North East Bab ($599m, 60 months) and Bu Hasa wellhead surface facilities ($392m EPC). A 12 Nov release says the three contracts were signed by Jereh's executive president and ADNOC Onshore's CEO (single source; the 4 Nov filing said unsigned). MEED expected a kick-off meeting later in November, with formal agreements due within 90 days of the start date.
